english: Let $L_1$ be the line $\overrightarrow{r}=(5\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+s(\hat{i}-\hat{k})$, $s\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $L_2$ be the line $\overrightarrow{r}=(3\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+5\hat{k})+t(2\hat{j}-\hat{k})$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$. As $P$ varies on $L_1$ and $Q$ varies on $L_2$, the locus of the mid-point of the segment $PQ$ is a plane which meets the $x$-axis, the $y$-axis and the $z$-axis at $(a,0,0)$, $(0,b,0)$ and $(0,0,c)$, respectively. Then the value of $a+b+c$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $L_1$ रेखा $\overrightarrow{r}=(5\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+s(\hat{i}-\hat{k})$, $s\in\mathbb{R}$ है, तथा $L_2$ रेखा $\overrightarrow{r}=(3\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+5\hat{k})+t(2\hat{j}-\hat{k})$, $t\in\mathbb{R}$ है। जब $P$ रेखा $L_1$ पर तथा $Q$ रेखा $L_2$ पर परिवर्तित होते हैं, तब रेखाखण्ड $PQ$ के मध्य-बिन्दु का बिन्दुपथ एक तल है जो $x$-अक्ष, $y$-अक्ष तथा $z$-अक्ष से क्रमशः $(a,0,0)$, $(0,b,0)$ तथा $(0,0,c)$ पर मिलता है। तब $a+b+c$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $P=(5+s,-1,3-s)$, $Q=(3,5+2t,5-t)$; mid-point $(h,k,l)$: $h=4+\dfrac s2,\ k=2+t,\ l=4-\dfrac s2-\dfrac t2$
Every $(h,k)$ comes from exactly one $(s,t)$, so the locus is the whole plane $2x+y+2z=18$ (normal $(1,0,-1)\times(0,2,-1)=(2,1,2)$, as expected)
solution_full: The mid-point $(h,k,l)$ of $PQ$ has $h=\dfrac{8+s}{2}=4+\dfrac s2$, $k=\dfrac{4+2t}{2}=2+t$, $l=\dfrac{8-s-t}{2}=4-\dfrac s2-\dfrac t2$.
From the first two, $s=2h-8$ and $t=k-2$. Substituting in the third: $l=4-(h-4)-\dfrac{k-2}{2}$, so $2l=16-2h-k+2$, that is $2h+k+2l=18$.

Conversely, for any $(h,k)$ the values $s=2h-8$, $t=k-2$ give a mid-point with that $h$, $k$ and with $l$ from the plane equation, so every point of the plane is attained. The locus is the plane $2x+y+2z=18$.

(This plane passes through the mid-point $(4,2,4)$ of the given points and is parallel to both lines; its normal is $(1,0,-1)\times(0,2,-1)=(2,1,2)$. The lines are skew because $(-2,6,2)\cdot(2,1,2)=6\neq0$.)
originality_note: New: the set of mid-points of all segments joining two skew lines is a plane parallel to both, found by eliminating the two parameters; the plane is then read through its intercepts (way 3). Closest known: locus of a point at a fixed relation to fixed points (PA^2 - PB^2 = k, a plane). Different because: the moving point depends on two independent points on two lines, and the plane arises from eliminating two parameters, not from cancelling squares.

concept_use.Locus problems in three dimensions: The mid-point of PQ is written with two parameters and both are eliminated, giving the locus 2x + y + 2z = 18 (and every point of it is attained).

stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line, vector and plane is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy/numpy, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Said that P and Q vary independently on their lines, so the locus is the full plane; the intercepts exist because all three coefficients are non-zero. Changed: replaced an earlier design (PA^2 + PB^2 = 2PC^2, whose 2D version is a published problem) by this one.
key_step: Writing the mid-point with two parameters and eliminating them to get the plane.
justification: Routine multi-step locus: parametrise, eliminate two parameters, read intercepts; no insight once the parametrisation is written. Like the routine vector-3D chain of 2026-P2-Q1 (L2), above the direct plane item 2024-P1-Q12 (L1).
